About the Role
PCP Solutions is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Graduate Civil Engineer to join our growing team.
This is an excellent opportunity for a recent engineering graduate or someone in the early stages of their career to gain valuable hands-on experience working on large-scale civil infrastructure projects.
Working alongside experienced Project Managers, Site Engineers and Supervisors, you will assist with the planning, coordination, quality assurance and delivery of civil construction works from commencement through to completion.
The successful applicant will be provided with ongoing guidance and support while developing their technical knowledge, project management skills and practical understanding of civil construction operations.
The Company
PCP Solutions is a leading civil earthworks and commercial plumbing business based in Toowoomba, delivering projects across South East Queensland.
With over 70 staff, PCP Solutions specialises in large-scale infrastructure works for Tier 1 contractors whilst maintaining a supportive, family-focused culture.
We pride ourselves on delivering quality projects, building strong working relationships and providing opportunities for our employees to grow and develop within the business.
Key Responsibilities
Working under the guidance of senior project personnel, your responsibilities will include:
- Assist with daily site inspections and monitoring construction activities.
- Prepare, maintain and complete Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and associated quality assurance documentation.
- Assist with the preparation and submission of project reports and documentation to Principal Contractors.
- Support daily work front reporting, progress tracking and construction records.
- Assist with project programming, scheduling and monitoring critical deadlines.
- Provide project administration and engineering support to Project Managers, Site Engineers, Supervisors and Quality and Safety personnel.
- Assist with reviewing construction drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
- Monitor supplier material conformance and ensure materials meet project specifications.
- Assist with quantity calculations, material take-offs and procurement requirements.
- Support the implementation and maintenance of project quality, workplace health and safety and environmental controls.
- Assist with identifying and reporting potential project risks, delays and construction issues.
- Maintain accurate project records, filing systems and document control processes.
- Provide regular project progress updates to the Project Manager and wider project team.
- Ensure compliance with the company's Integrated Management System (IMS), policies and procedures.
Skills and Qualifications
We are looking for someone who is eager to learn, takes initiative and is passionate about developing a career in civil construction.
The successful applicant will ideally possess:
- A completed Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
- Recent graduates and applicants with up to 2 years of industry experience are encouraged to apply.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work professionally with clients, suppliers, subcontractors and site personnel.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate documentation.
- A willingness to learn and develop practical construction and project management skills.
- Basic understanding of civil construction methods, engineering drawings and specifications.
- Sound computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- Ability to work independently when required and contribute positively to a team environment.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a strong commitment to workplace safety.
- A current driver's licence and Construction White Card, or willingness to obtain a White Card prior to commencing.
- Willingness to travel to regional project locations as required.
Previous experience in civil construction, earthworks, water infrastructure or quality assurance will be highly regarded but is not essential.
What We Offer
- Opportunity to gain hands-on experience on major civil infrastructure projects.
- Mentoring and ongoing support from experienced engineering and construction professionals.
- Exposure to Tier 1 construction projects and industry-leading systems.
- Career development and progression opportunities within a growing company.
- A supportive, family-focused team environment.
- Competitive remuneration based on qualifications and experience.
- A diverse role offering both site-based and project administration experience.
How to Apply
If you are a motivated Graduate Civil Engineer looking to kick-start your career and gain practical experience in the civil construction industry, we would love to hear from you.
Apply via SEEK or email your resume and cover letter to admin@pcpsolutions.com.au
Join PCP Solutions and build your engineering career with a team committed to quality, safety and delivering successful projects.

- Demonstrated experience delivering FRP and concrete works

- The ability to coordinate multiple work fronts and keep projects moving

- The ability to work autonomously, make decisions and take ownership of your work

Kick-start your career in Civil Design with one of the region’s largest and most diverse infrastructure portfolios!
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Cadet Designer to join our Design & Survey Services team. This is an exciting opportunity to earn while you learn, gain hands-on industry experience, and build a rewarding career in civil engineering and infrastructure design.
Our Ideal Candidate:
We are seeking a Cadet Designer who is eager to learn and willing to dedicate themselves to continuous development within a technically focused environment. The ideal candidate will have completed Year 12 or hold a Certificate III in Engineering and be qualified for acceptance into an Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil) course, or an equivalent qualification. They will demonstrate a detail-oriented mindset, strong analytical skills, and a willingness to integrate into and contribute positively to the established team culture. A current "C" Class Driver's Licence is required, with the ability to independently drive between business locations to meet operational needs. The successful candidate will also maintain a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes for the Cairns community.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Undertake training in the use of civil design software (AutoCAD, 12d Model and relevant GIS systems).
- Undertake training in the investigation, planning, development and delivery of civil design projects.
- Develop knowledge and understanding of relevant standards, guidelines and legislative documents (e.g. Austroads, Queensland Urban Drainage Manual, Queensland Streets, Main Roads technical publications and Australian Standards).
- Assist with field investigations, traffic surveys and stakeholder consultation associated with allocated projects.
- Preparation of detailed civil design drawings and estimates for a range of multi-disciplinary infrastructure projects with guidance and as directed.
- Provide general administrative assistance such as database maintenance and document control using established procedures.
- Develop an approach to contributing technical knowledge and innovative problem solutions to design activities.
Study Allowances
Council provides paid study and examination leave, along with course fee reimbursements, to support your professional development and ensure success in your university studies.
Why Join the Design Team?
Supportive Team Environment
Our team combines professionalism with a relaxed and supportive culture. We value collaboration, open communication, and the occasional good-natured banter. We pride ourselves on fostering an environment where people can enjoy coming to work and working together to achieve quality outcomes.
Professional Growth and Development
The team provides excellent opportunities for learning and career development. Graduates, cadets and even experienced professionals benefit from mentorship, knowledge sharing and support from highly experienced staff.
Unique Lifestyle Benefits
Based in Cairns, we benefit from the unique lifestyle provided by the area. Nestled between the reef and rainforest, the region offers an abundance of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors and maintain a healthy work-life balance.
Diverse and Meaningful Projects
Our project portfolio is varied and challenging, providing opportunities to work across multiple disciplines and asset types. No two projects are the same, and team members take pride in delivering infrastructure that benefits the local community.
Some benefits we offer:
- Achieve work / life balance with flexible working arrangements
- Fitness Passport - subsidised health and well-being memberships (gym/swimming pool)
- Recharge with up to 5 weeks annual leave
- Up to 3 weeks personal leave
- Cherish family time with up to 14 weeks paid parental leave
- Grow personally and professionally with learning and development opportunities
- Salary sacrifice opportunities
- Up to $5,000 study assistance per annum (inclusive of Fringe Benefits Tax) towards the cost of your Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil)
We are committed to:
- Fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment
- Embracing innovation and continuous improvement
- Cultivating a culture of professional growth and support

candidates.content_text:
Build infrastructure that keeps Queensland moving!
Are you a civil engineer ready to apply your technical knowledge to meaningful transport projects? Join Transport and Main Roads and help plan, deliver and manage roads, bridges and other infrastructure that support safe and reliable travel across Central Queensland.
About the role
As a Civil Engineer, you will work with experienced engineering and project professionals across the full project lifecycle. You will contribute to transport planning, project development, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management activities, while building your capability under the guidance of senior engineering staff.
Central Queensland Region manages transport infrastructure across more than 600,000 square kilometres, including over 9,000 kilometres of state-controlled roads and 1,500 kilometres of the National Land Transport Network. With offices in Rockhampton, Mackay, Emerald and Barcaldine, the region offers exposure to varied infrastructure, environments and engineering challenges.
In this role, you will:
* provide technical engineering advice and undertake assessments to support planning, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management
* manage projects or project components to achieve quality outcomes, value for money and sound engineering practice
* identify project risks, emerging issues and opportunities, and develop practical and cost-effective solutions
* support procurement activities and the administration of consultant and construction contracts
* coordinate budgets, forecasting, accruals, procurement and performance reporting
* contribute to the delivery of road, bridge, maintenance and asset improvement projects
* build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders
* ensure work meets relevant governance, safety, risk management and departmental requirements.
What you will bring
You will use sound judgement, take responsibility for the quality of your work and collaborate effectively to achieve project outcomes. You will be comfortable applying civil engineering and project management principles across multiple infrastructure projects, while actively developing your professional knowledge and capability.
You must hold:
* a four-year Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering, or an equivalent qualification accepted by Engineers Australia
* a current Class C driver licence.
Why join TMR?
You will gain hands-on experience across diverse transport infrastructure projects while working alongside experienced professionals. TMR supports career development, an inclusive workplace and a healthy work-life balance.
This role provides an opportunity to strengthen your technical, project management, commercial and stakeholder engagement skills while contributing to infrastructure that makes a practical difference for Queensland communities.
If you are looking for varied civil engineering work, professional support and the opportunity to contribute across the full project lifecycle, we encourage you to apply.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.

As demand for advanced computing and AI infrastructure continues to accelerate, Intravision is expanding its involvement in some of the industry's most complex digital infrastructure projects. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to major developments across the Data Centre and hyperscale sectors, including next-generation facilities supporting AI workloads and large-scale GPU computing.
Working across our national operations, you will support our ACT, Sydney, Melbourne and New Zealand teams, partnering with colleagues across estimating, operations and project delivery. The position can be based in either our ACT, Sydney or Melbourne office.

- Supporting estimating activities across Intravision's ACT, Sydney, Melbourne and New Zealand operations.
- Preparing cost estimates for fibre, copper and structured cabling works.
- Analysing tender documentation, technical specifications, drawings and project requirements.
- Undertaking detailed material, equipment and labour take-offs.
- Developing labour allowances, installation approaches and project cost breakdowns.
- Evaluating supplier and subcontractor quotations to establish competitive project pricing.
- Reviewing tender requirements to identify discrepancies, scope gaps and commercial risks.
- Preparing pricing schedules, tender qualifications and supporting submission documentation.
- Liaising with internal stakeholders to validate costs, resources and project assumptions.
- Contributing to estimating strategies and supporting the successful pursuit of major project opportunities.

- Minimum 5 years' experience in estimating telecommunications, communications, structured cabling or ICT infrastructure projects.
- Strong technical knowledge of fibre optic and copper cabling systems.
- Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, cable schedules and bills of quantities.
- Experience preparing detailed cost estimates and competitive tender submissions.
- Understanding of installation methodologies, labour productivity and project costing.
- Experience in Data Centres, hyperscale or other mission-critical environments will be highly regarded.
- Exposure to AI infrastructure, GPU cluster deployments and high-density computing environments will be advantageous.
Core Attributes
- Strong commercial judgement and analytical thinking.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Strong organisation and time management, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
- A collaborative approach and confidence working with teams across multiple locations.
- Proactive problem-solving skills and the ability to identify risks and develop practical solutions.
- Ability to work independently, take ownership and meet deadlines.
Apply Now!
Ready to take your estimating career into the next generation of digital infrastructure? Join Intravision and help deliver the connectivity supporting tomorrow's AI and hyperscale environments.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

candidates.content_text:
Design the future of a growing city.
Help shape how Blacktown City manages the parks, playgrounds, sportsfields and recreation assets our community uses every day.
As Asset Engineer, you manage asset information and turn condition, risk, utilisation and service data into practical maintenance, renewal and capital programs. You validate asset registers, coordinate condition and compliance inspections, maintain the Open Space Asset Management Plan and develop a 20-year renewal forecast. You also identify renewal backlogs and prioritise projects based on risk, utilisation and service needs.
Within Asset Planning and Support, you prepare annual renewal and long-term financial plan inputs, develop lifecycle strategies for playgrounds, sportsfields and park structures, and support renewal scopes and asset handovers. You also contribute to works programs, tender assessments, grants, contribution plans, works-in-kind agreements and statutory reporting.
Your work helps Council understand when assets need attention and where investment has the greatest value for the community.
At Blacktown City Council, good people make great teams, and great teams build great cities. Here, you will find the stability and support to keep growing, along with:
 - a term contract, full-time role for up to 2 years with one of Australia's largest councils 
 - an entry level salary commencing at $2,257.27 per week
 - a 35-hour working week 
 - a leaseback vehicle
 - access to Council's flextime arrangement
 - 12% superannuation and competitive leave entitlements
 - ongoing training and development support
 - access to Fitness Passport, social clubs and wellbeing programs.
 Our commitment to safety
Blacktown City Council is committed to safety. We have introduced alcohol and other drug testing at the pre-employment phase, and via a series of random and cause testing.
We are a child safe organisation that supports and promotes the safety, wellbeing and empowerment of children.

candidates.content_text:
About Flow
Flow Infrastructure is a specialist design and construct firm delivering water and wastewater treatment infrastructure, including water and sewage treatment plants, pump stations, recycled water schemes and industrial wastewater systems. Our sister company, Flow Utilities, operates and maintains the assets we deliver. Our clients include developers, councils, government and industry across South Australia and interstate.
Flow was established in 2026 by a team that has worked together for more than 20 years. Collectively we bring more than 80 years of experience and, in previous roles, our team delivered 37 sewage treatment plants, with project experience across Australia and New Zealand. Flow is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 and holds a building work contractors licence specific to sewer and water infrastructure installation.
Current projects include industrial and winery wastewater treatment, private water and sewerage schemes for greenfield communities, and municipal treatment plant upgrades, delivered for developers, industry, councils and government.
The role
You will prepare design and construction documentation across our water and wastewater projects, working jointly with our Design Lead on mechanical, piping and plant layout drafting and with our Electrical and Automation Lead on electrical and control documentation.
You will be involved from tender through detailed design, construction and as constructed records, working closely with our process and design engineers so that every drawing set is accurate, coordinated and buildable. You will:
- Prepare 2D drawings and 3D models for sewage and water treatment plants, pump stations, recycled water schemes and industrial wastewater systems.
- Produce general arrangements, plant layouts, piping arrangements and isometrics using AutoCAD and Plant 3D.
- Prepare tank, skid and fabrication drawings, along with valve, pump and instrument schedules.
- Prepare site layouts, pipeline and rising main alignments, long sections and services coordination drawings using Civil 3D.
- Draft P&IDs and process flow diagrams with our process engineers.
- Prepare electrical and control documentation, including single line diagrams, schematics, switchboard layouts and cable routes, under the direction of the Electrical and Automation Lead.
- Coordinate drawing inputs from suppliers, subcontractors and our civil and structural design partner.
- Prepare drawing sets for tenders, regulatory submissions, construction and as constructed records.
- Manage drawing registers and revision control, and help develop the CAD templates, blocks and standards for the business.
- Attend site during construction and commissioning as required, including measurement and as constructed checks.
About you
- Proven experience as a mechanical or process plant drafter. A Diploma or Advanced Diploma of Engineering (Drafting) is valued, but your portfolio matters more than your qualifications.
- At least 5 years of drafting experience in the water sector or comparable process plant work, ideally on water and wastewater treatment plants, pump stations or pipeline infrastructure. Applicants whose background is in residential, commercial building or architectural drafting are not suited to this position and will not be considered.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Plant 3D is essential. Experience in Inventor or SolidWorks is an advantage.
- Construction experience is beneficial but not essential. It helps to understand how drawings turn into steel, pipe and concrete.
- Experience preparing P&IDs, piping arrangements and plant layouts, with a working knowledge of valves, pumps, pipework, instruments, tanks and dosing systems. Electrical and control drafting experience is highly regarded.
- Careful and organised, with good drawing control habits and a sound understanding of drafting standards.
- The ability to manage several projects at once.
- Clear communication skills, with the confidence to work with engineers, suppliers and site teams.
- Willing to undertake site visits within South Australia and occasional interstate travel as required.
What we offer
- A salary of $100k to $125k plus super, depending on experience.
- An equal share of company profits alongside every other permanent employee.
- Broad exposure across municipal and industrial water and wastewater projects, from design through construction and operation, with process, mechanical, electrical and automation design all delivered in house.
- Varied, hands on project work, and the opportunity to shape the drafting standards and templates of a growing business.
- A collaborative, experienced team where you work closely with the business owners and have a direct say in decisions.
- A modern office on Grote Street in the Adelaide CBD.
How to apply
Please include your CV, a cover letter and a selection of sample drawings or models with your application, with any confidential client information removed. Make sure your application accurately reflects your own experience and qualifications. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to talk through their work at interview and may be asked to complete a short practical drafting exercise. Applications that are clearly AI generated or overstate experience will not be progressed.
You must have current Australian working rights.

- Collaborate with passionate people who bring a "boots & all" attitude to everything they do

SEE Civil is seeking experienced Project Engineers and Site Engineers to join our construction teams delivering TMR and Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA) projects in the Mt Tamborine region.
These are full-time opportunities where you will support the technical and engineering delivery of road infrastructure, reconstruction, rehabilitation and disaster recovery works.
Working closely with the Project Manager, Senior Project Engineer and site teams, you will assist with project programming procurement, subcontractor coordination, quality assurance, safety, cost control and the day-to-day technical requirements of project delivery.
You will work across both site and project activities, supporting the team to ensure works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project specifications, contractual requirements, relevant Australian Standards and TMR requirements. 
Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the planning, coordination and delivery of engineering activities and site works across TMR and DRFA projects.
- Support the development, monitoring and updating of project programs to achieve key milestones and delivery targets.
- Coordinate subcontractors, procurement, materials, plant and equipment required for project delivery.
- Provide technical support to construction teams and assist with resolving engineering, construction and design issues.
- Review engineering drawings, specifications and construction methodologies to support safe and efficient project delivery.
- Assist with quality assurance activities, including ITPs, inspections, testing, quality records and project documentation.
- Ensure works are completed in accordance with project specifications, relevant legislation, Australian Standards, contractual obligations and applicable TMR requirements.
- Prepare and maintain project documentation, including technical submissions, requests for information, site records, progress reporting and other engineering documentation.
- Assist with contract administration, procurement, subcontractor management, variations and scope changes.
- Monitor project quantities, costs and productivity and contribute to project forecasts and reporting.
- Conduct site inspections and monitor construction activities to ensure compliance with quality, safety and environmental requirements.
- Identify engineering, constructability and project delivery issues and work with the wider project team to develop practical solutions.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Contribute to a positive and collaborative project environment focused on safety, quality and successful project delivery.
Essential Skills and Attributes
- Demonstrated engineering experience within the civil construction industry.
- Previous experience as a Project Engineer, Site Engineer or Graduate Engineer within a civil construction environment.
- Experience across road infrastructure, reconstruction, rehabilitation, earthworks, drainage, structures or associated civil works will be highly regarded.
- Previous exposure to TMR projects and/or DRFA-funded disaster recovery works will be highly regarded.
- Sound understanding of engineering principles and practical civil construction methodologies.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, designs, specifications and relevant Australian Standards.
- Experience with or an understanding of quality assurance processes, including ITPs, inspections and construction documentation.
- Strong planning, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to coordinate subcontractors, suppliers and site activities to support project delivery.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across project and construction teams.
- Sound commercial awareness and an understanding of project costs, quantities, procurement and variations.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to safety, quality and successful project outcomes.
- Computer literacy, including Microsoft Office applications and project management systems
Qualifications
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or an equivalent recognized engineering discipline.
- Current driver licence.
- Current Construction White Card.
What's next?
If you are a Project Engineer or Site Engineer looking to develop your career while working on significant road infrastructure and disaster recovery projects, we’d love to hear from you.
If you hold full, unlimited working rights in Australia, we encourage you to submit your CV by selecting Apply Now.
As an Equal Opportunity Employer, women and people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander heritage are strongly encouraged to apply.

candidates.content_text:
Lift Engineer – Mobile Crane Industry
Department: Engineering / Operations
Reports To: General Manager
Location: Narre Warren
We are currently sourcing a Lift Engineer to join our Crane Tech team.
Our company specialises in Mobile Crane hire and lifting services for builders, civil contractors and industrial businesses across Melbourne and Gippsland.
We are seeking a Lift Engineer to be responsible for the preparation of lift studies, engineered lift plans and technical assessments for mobile crane operations. This role would potentially suit a Graduate Engineer.
The role ensures that lifting operations are properly planned, technically sound and compliant with relevant Australian Standards, WHS legislation and company procedures.
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare lift studies and engineered lift plans for mobile crane operations.
- Determine suitable crane types, capacities and configurations for lifting requirements.
- Undertake engineering calculations relating to load weights, lifting capacities, crane radii and boom configurations.
- Calculate outrigger loads, ground-bearing pressures and ground support requirements.
- Review engineering drawings, site plans and project specifications.
- Assess lifting requirements and identify potential risks and operational limitations.
- Develop safe and practical lifting methodologies for complex lifting operations.
- Provide technical advice and engineering support to Project Managers, Crane Supervisors and operational personnel.
- Liaise with clients, contractors and external engineers regarding lifting requirements.
- Prepare and maintain accurate engineering documentation, calculations and lift plans.
- Ensure all engineering work complies with relevant Australian Standards, WHS legislation and company procedures.
- Identify and escalate any engineering concerns or unsafe lifting arrangements.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential:
- Relevant tertiary engineering qualification, preferably Mechanical, Civil or Structural Engineering.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation.
- Strong computer skills and attention to detail.
Desirable:
- Experience with crane planning and lift simulation software.
- Experience with complex and critical lifting operations.
- Experience in the crane or heavy lifting industry.
- Strong understanding of mobile crane operations and crane load charts.
- Experience preparing lift studies and engineered lift plans.
- Knowledge of crane configurations, load calculations and ground-bearing pressures.
- Knowledge of relevant Australian Standards and WHS requirements.
Skills and Competencies
- Strong technical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Effective communication and problem-solving abilities.
- Strong organisational and time management skills.
- Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
- A strong commitment to workplace health and safety.
If this sounds like you and you would like to join our friendly and fun team, please submit your CV today.
Please note only Australian residents will be considered for this position.
